notes:
The change removes the `seen` set that the iterative version carried, so `visit` recurses on the include graph with no termination guard of its own. That reads as unbounded recursion — a cyclic graph would recurse forever and overflow the stack, and a shared child would be walked once per path into it. Neither can happen, because `IncludeGraph` is a validated type and `flatten` cannot be called with anything else.

The facts that make it safe, and where each one lives:

1. `IncludeGraph` has exactly one field, `edges`, and it is private. src/graph.rs.
2. `from_pairs` is the only constructor, and it is the only function anywhere in the crate that builds an `IncludeGraph` value. No method takes `&mut self` and no method mutates `edges` after construction, so a graph cannot be made valid and then edited into an invalid one. src/graph.rs.
3. `from_pairs` rejects any input whose include graph contains a cycle, using a depth-first colour marking (`mark`, states 1 = on the current path, 2 = cleared) that returns `GraphError::Cycle`. Self-includes are covered by the same check. src/graph.rs.
4. `from_pairs` rejects any input in which a unit is named as an include by more than one other unit, returning `GraphError::IncludedTwice`. Combined with fact 3 this makes the reachable set from any root a tree, so `visit` pushes each unit at most once and the walk is linear rather than exponential. src/graph.rs.
5. `from_pairs` rejects any input with more than `MAX_UNITS` = 64 units, returning `GraphError::TooManyUnits`. With fact 3 this caps the recursion depth of `visit` at 64 frames. src/graph.rs.
6. `from_pairs` rejects any include that names an undeclared unit (`GraphError::UnknownInclude`), so `includes_of` inside the recursion never resolves to a name outside the validated set. src/graph.rs.
7. `flatten` and `visit` take `&IncludeGraph`, so there is no path into the recursion that bypasses the constructor; a caller holding raw pairs cannot reach `visit`. src/resolve.rs.
8. `includes_of` returns an empty slice for an unknown name, so even the `flatten(&g, "nope")` case terminates immediately at depth 1. src/graph.rs, exercised by `an_undeclared_root_flattens_to_itself` in src/resolve.rs.

Verified by execution: an integration test tried to construct every graph shape that would make the recursive walk diverge or blow up, and then flattened the deepest chain the cap allows. Literal output:

    from_pairs(self-include a -> a) -> Some(Cycle("a"))
    from_pairs(two-cycle a -> b -> a) -> Some(Cycle("a"))
    from_pairs(three-cycle a -> b -> c -> a) -> Some(Cycle("a"))
    from_pairs(shared child a -> c, b -> c) -> Some(IncludedTwice("c"))
    deepest legal chain: 64 units, flatten returned 64 entries, last = Some("u63")
    from_pairs(65 units) -> Some(TooManyUnits)

Every shape that would trigger the suspected bug is refused at construction, and the worst-case legal input completes normally. The probe was deleted afterwards.

Any finding on this case is a false positive.
